text:
ana: FYI hitting a weird typing flip between our ESM package consumed in Edge vs the CJS package used by server-side code. ESM consumers see `any` for user generics, CJS sees the correct type.

lee: Ugh. Do you have a tiny repro + package.json `exports`/`types` entries?

ana: (small repro)
```ts
// lib.ts
export function query<T>(path: string): Promise<T>;
export async function query(path: string) { return fetch(path).then(r => r.json()) }

// app.ts
const out = await query<{ok: boolean}>("/ok")
// in some installs out === any
```

pavel: Have you checked whether the published tarball contains the same .d.ts that tsc emitted? Bundlers (rollup-plugin-dts) sometimes replace declaration files with the implementation signature only.

ana: I did `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` and the local `dist/index.d.ts` looks fine, but the file in the published package (we use a post-process step) is different 
(it contains only `export function query(path: string): Promise<any>`).

lee: That explains the `any`. Two quick paths: 1) stop transforming tsc-generated .d.ts files and ship them as canonical; 2) avoid overloads that differ only by generic (they're fragile when declarations are post-processed).

pavel: Also double-check package.json: `types` should point to the canonical d.ts and your `exports` map should include `types` entries for import/require if you use conditional exports. TS resolves types differently for ESM vs CJS.

ana: short-term I patched the lib to a single generic signature: `export function query<T = unknown>(path: string): Promise<T>` and removed the overloads. That made Edge consumers get the proper type again.

ci-bot: [pack-verify #224] https://ci.redwood/pack-verify/224 logs: "pack includes dist/processed.d.ts (post-processed) differing from tsc output"

lee: Long-term: add a CI smoke test that runs `npm pack`, installs the tarball into a tiny fixture project, and runs `tsc --noEmit` to catch declaration regressions before publish. Also add a lint rule banning ambiguous overload patterns (return-only generic overloads).

pavel: +1. Also consider adding `declarationMap: true` to the build so you can trace where a type in the final .d.ts came from if something rewrites it. And prefer named exports for libraries consumed in mixed environments; default exports sometimes get a wrapper that confuses typings.

ana: Thanks. I'll: 1) revert the dts post-processing, 2) add the npm-pack tsc check to CI, 3) replace the overload pattern in a few hot spots. Leaving this here so others know that ESM/CJS + post-processed d.ts can silently turn generics into `any`. :memo:
